winner.premise: A woman discovers that the roommate who handles the apartment bills has been collecting a fake monthly maintenance fee from everyone while repeatedly paying the real rent late.
winner.conflict: The narrator and another roommate trust the bill-paying roommate's claim that a separate maintenance fee is required, until the landlord confirms the fee does not exist and reveals that the actual rent has also been paid late.
winner.twist: The roommate posing as the responsible household money manager has been pocketing the invented fee and is exposed when the landlord arrives over late rent despite everyone else paying her early.
winner.hook: My roommate charged us a fake building fee for six months—then the landlord knocked on our door asking why the rent was late.
winner.narration:
For the first two months, I didn't question it because my roommate had lived there longer and handled all the bills. On the first of every month, she'd drop a message in our group chat: rent, utilities, and a two-hundred-dollar "building maintenance fee" that had to be transferred to her separately.

She said the landlord collected it in cash for cleaning, lift servicing, and "shared-area wear." It sounded weird, but she always made it sound official. She'd even remind us that late payment could affect our lease renewal.

By month four, I noticed something strange. The lobby noticeboard listed the building's actual maintenance charges, and tenants weren't responsible for any extra monthly fee. I asked her about it. She immediately said our unit had a "special arrangement" because our rent was discounted.

That answer bothered me, so I emailed the landlord asking for the fee schedule. He replied with one sentence: "There is no separate maintenance fee for your unit."

I showed the other roommate. Together, we'd paid almost twenty-four hundred dollars in fake fees.

Before we confronted her, the landlord unexpectedly knocked on our door. He looked annoyed and asked why that month's rent was already ten days late.

My roommate rushed into the hallway and tried to tell him there had been a banking delay. Then he opened his tablet and showed us the payment history. The full rent had been late three times, even though both of us had always transferred our shares to her early.

So I asked, right in front of him, where our extra maintenance money had been going.

She froze.

First she said it was for household expenses. Then she said she'd planned to pay everyone back. Then she claimed she had misunderstood the lease.

The landlord asked to see the messages where she said he required the fee. I handed him my phone.

He read them twice, looked at her, and said, "I never told you to collect any of this."

She started crying and saying we were making her look like a criminal over a misunderstanding.

I finally said, "You invented a fee and forgot to pay the real rent."

That was the moment the excuses stopped.

The landlord removed her as the payment contact, split future rent payments between us directly, and gave her thirty days to repay every dollar she'd collected.

She'd spent six months acting like the responsible roommate.

Turns out, she was the only bill we needed to audit.
winner.title: My Roommate Invented a Fake Rent Fee
winner.description: My roommate handled every bill and made a mysterious monthly building fee sound completely official. Then the landlord showed up asking why the real rent was late—and the entire story fell apart.
winner.payoff: You invented a fee and forgot to pay the real rent.
